oil.summary: Crude gave back some of last week's sharp geopolitical premium today — WTI slipped 1.46% to $78.44 and Brent eased 0.69% to $84.31 — though both benchmarks remain roughly 9-11% higher on the week, reflecting the Hormuz risk-on surge that followed Iranian missile strikes on Emirati tankers and the US resumption of an Iranian port blockade. The more notable move was RBOB gasoline, off 6.23% in a single session, suggesting some demand-side anxiety or speculative unwind. Heating oil held firmer, still up 20% on the month. TotalEnergies flagged stronger Q2 refining margins and trading profits, consistent with the volatile spread environment. On policy, a US bill targeting India and China with 100% tariffs on Russian oil imports adds a secondary-sanctions overhang, while India's growing refining footprint could partially reroute flows.
drivers: Iranian missile strikes on Emirati tankers and US port blockade of Iran drove an ~10% weekly spike in Brent; partial profit-taking today
RBOB gasoline -6.23% on the day was the sharpest single-session mover, diverging significantly from crude
Proposed US 100% tariffs on Indian and Chinese purchases of Russian crude introduce a new trade-flow disruption risk

gas.summary: The Henry Hub/TTF divergence is stark and widening. Henry Hub fell 1.16% to $2.89/MMBtu and is down over 8% on the month, reflecting ample domestic US supply. TTF, by contrast, surged 1.74% to €55.3/MWh and is up 30% over the past month, driven entirely by Hormuz-related LNG supply fears. Asian LNG spot prices jumped 10% on the week as Qatari supply falters amid the conflict, with Pakistan forced to pay a four-year high for a spot cargo. Dana Gas suspended all operations at Iraq's Khor Mor field citing credible security threats, removing additional supply from an already stressed market. Ukraine's strike on Russia's last gas refinery adds a further upstream disruption vector. The EU's new Electrification Action Plan targets 46% electricity share by 2040, a structural headwind for long-run gas demand in Europe.
drivers: Hormuz conflict disrupting Qatari LNG flows: Asian spot prices +10% on the week, Pakistan pays four-year high for spot cargo
Dana Gas suspends Khor Mor field operations amid security threats, tightening regional gas supply further
Henry Hub -8% on the month amid ample US supply, underscoring a deepening Atlantic Basin price divergence

power.summary: EU carbon slipped 2.66% to $74.78/EUA today, essentially flat on the week and month, suggesting the carbon market is not yet pricing the Hormuz disruption as a significant structural fuel-switching catalyst despite TTF's 30% monthly surge. The divergence is notable: higher gas costs in Europe typically lift coal and carbon burn, which would support EUAs, but that transmission appears muted today. The EU's newly announced Electrification Action Plan — targeting electricity at 46% of total energy by 2040 — is a long-term carbon-supportive signal but carries no near-term price impulse. Broader geopolitical rewiring, including the Eni CEO's comments on capital shifting to Southeast Asia and Latin America away from the Gulf, and a reported power vacuum reshaping Eurasian trade routes, point to structural shifts in where future generation investment flows.
drivers: EUA -2.66% on the day despite TTF's 30% monthly surge; fuel-switching pressure not yet transmitting into carbon prices
EU Electrification Action Plan targets 46% electricity share of final consumption by 2040, a structural long-run support for carbon demand
Eni and industry peers shifting capex to Southeast Asia and Latin America amid sustained Hormuz disruption, reshaping future supply geography
